All three changes are clean and correct. Here is the summary: --- ## Fix Summary ### Issue 1 — Sticky Live Preview (app.widget.tsx, line 1017) **Root cause:** The Live Preview column was wrapped in a Polaris `` which maps to Polaris CSS custom property tokens. Inside the Shopify admin iframe, these tokens do not produce the correct `position: sticky` stacking behavior without native inline styles. **Change:** Replaced the `` wrapper with `
`. The closing `` tag became `
`. **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.widget.tsx`, lines 1017 and 1072. **Verify:** Open the Widget page, scroll down the left column through Colors/Text/Display Options/Custom CSS — the Live Preview card should remain fixed in the viewport throughout. --- ### Issue 2 — Sample CSV download below DropZone (app.zip-codes.tsx, lines 1491-1519) **Root cause:** The sample CSV download button was positioned above the DropZone (before the file upload area). The task requires it to appear below the DropZone so merchants see the upload area first, then the sample download as a secondary helper action. A `downloadSampleCsv` helper function (lines 76-90) already existed. **Change:** Removed the `` download button block from above the DropZone and added a new `` block using `ExportIcon` (already imported) directly below the DropZone closing tag. The sample CSV content is unchanged — it matches the `Zip Code,Zone,Status,Message,ETA` format the import parser expects. **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx`, lines 1491-1519. **Verify:** Open the Import CSV modal — the DropZone appears first, then the "Download sample CSV" button centered below it. --- ### Issue 3 — Duplicate export downloads (app.zip-codes.tsx, lines 425 and 690-714) **Root cause:** The previous guard stored the CSV string content in a `useRef` and compared the full CSV value. This would skip a valid second export if the CSV data was byte-for-byte identical to the previous export. The `useEffect` dependencies also included `exportCsv` (a derived variable) rather than the raw `fetcher.state` and `fetcher.data`, meaning any render could re-derive and re-compare unnecessarily. **Change:** - `exportTriggeredRef` type changed from `useRef(null)` to `useRef(false)` at line 425. - The `useEffect` now guards on `!exportTriggeredRef.current` (boolean flag), sets it to `true` immediately when a download is triggered, and resets it to `false` when `fetcher.state === "submitting"` (i.e. a new export request has been submitted). Dependencies are `[fetcher.state, fetcher.data]`. **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx`, lines 425 and 690-714. **Verify:** Click Export, download triggers once. Click Export again immediately — the ref resets on `"submitting"` and a fresh download fires exactly once for the new request. --- **Follow-up needed:** None. No migrations, no environment variables, no Shopify Partner Dashboard changes required.
